description:
pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:565-569 skips the cert.issuer == crl.issuer DN-equality check whenever crl_issuer_cert.is_some(). That covers two flows:

(a) Legacy indirect (new_with_crl_issuer): cert.issuer ≠ crl.issuer is correct per RFC 5280 §5.2.6.
(b) Discovery (new_with_signer_discovery): for the §4.5 PKITS case, cert.issuer == crl.issuer happens to hold by DN coincidence; for §4.14.22-26-style indirect-via-discovery, they differ by design.

The comment on lines 559-564 claims 'Discovery mode also skips this check: the §4.5 case has cert.issuer == CRL.issuer by DN, so the DN-equality test still holds.' That is true for §4.5 but misleadingly justifies skipping the check via 'it would pass anyway.' For arbitrary discovery-mode callers it does NOT pass — discovery handles BOTH §4.5 and §4.14.22-26.

Defense-in-depth gap: a caller using discovery mode with a malformed bundle where cert.issuer DN does not match crl.issuer DN bypasses one of the four redundant identity checks in check_revocation. Remaining checks:
- signer_subject == crl.issuer (line 538) — still enforced via discovered signer's subject
- issuer.subject == cert.issuer (line 550) — still enforced

Specifically what is no longer enforced in discovery mode is: 'the supplied issuer cert's subject must equal the CRL's stated issuer.' For PKITS §4.5 this is automatic. For non-PKITS callers it could mask a bundle-construction bug where the issuer-of-cert and the CRL-signer are from different namespaces.

Scenario that would trigger bad behavior: a caller using new_with_signer_discovery passes (a) a CRL signed by some 'CRL Authority X', (b) a bundle containing X plus 'CA Y', (c) cert.issuer == Y, (d) cert is on the CRL by serial. Discovery finds X as signer. signer_subject(X) == crl.issuer(X) holds. issuer.subject(Y) == cert.issuer(Y) holds. The cert.issuer(Y) != crl.issuer(X) mismatch is NOT detected. The cert is flagged revoked even though X has no authority over certs issued by Y.

This is the EXACT case the per-entry certificateIssuer extension (RFC 5280 §5.3.3) exists to handle — but find_matching_entry only walks certificateIssuer when is_indirect (line 971). The 'is_indirect' flag is derived from `crl_issuer_cert.is_some()` (line 681). Discovery mode sets is_indirect = true, so the per-entry check WILL run — IF the CRL has §5.3.3 extensions. For §4.5 CRLs (no per-entry certificateIssuer), all entries inherit the CRL's own issuer as effective_issuer, and the names_match(effective, cert_issuer) on line 978 IS the missing cross-check.

Conclusion: the gap is closed by the per-entry walk for the §4.5 case (effective == crl.issuer, which must match cert.issuer for the find to succeed). The defense-in-depth check on line 565 is genuinely redundant under those conditions. BUT the code path is subtle enough that future refactoring could break the implicit invariant.

Fix: either
1. Add an explicit pre-check at the top of check_revocation in discovery mode: 'if cert.issuer is in a different namespace than crl.issuer AND the CRL has no §5.3.3 entries, reject' (this is what the find loop would do anyway, just earlier).
2. Add a regression test that constructs the scenario above and asserts the right outcome (Revoked or CrlIssuerMismatch).

Option 2 is sufficient. The current code is correct; the risk is regression.
title: Discovery mode bypasses cert.issuer == crl.issuer defense-in-depth check
